suites.title: 1. Primary user flow — JRN-01.1: Daily Expense Capture

specs.title: Maya opens the expense tracker in her browser
She sees an empty list inviting her to add her first expense
She sees the entry form with amount, description and category fields
She types the amount, what she bought, and the category
She clicks Add Expense and her latte appears in the list
She sees the running total pick up the new expense
She gets a confirmation and a cleared form ready for the next entry
Spotting a typo, she clicks Edit and the form fills with the current values
She can tell she is editing — the button says Save Changes and Cancel appears
She corrects the amount, saves, and the row shows the corrected value
She sees the total recalculate to match the correction
After saving she is confirmed and the form is back to adding new expenses
The form offers amount, description, category and a submit button
The amount field accepts a value with two decimal places
Description accepts up to 500 characters and category up to 100
The form cannot be submitted with any field empty
A success indicator confirms the expense was saved
After each submission the form clears and focus returns to amount
Twenty expenses entered in sequence all appear in the list with an accurate total
Each expense is persisted server-side before success is shown (no client-only cache)
Closing the tab mid-session loses nothing already submitted

suites.title: US-0.3: Receive Validation Feedback on Expense Entry

specs.title: An empty amount shows "Amount is required"
A non-numeric amount shows "Amount must be a valid number"
A zero or negative amount shows "Amount must be greater than zero"
An amount above 999,999.99 shows "Amount must not exceed 999,999.99"
An amount with three decimals shows "Amount must have at most two decimal places"
An empty description shows "Description is required"
A description over 500 characters shows "Description must not exceed 500 characters"
An empty category shows "Category is required"
A category over 100 characters shows "Category must not exceed 100 characters"
The form keeps what the user typed when validation fails
Several invalid fields show all their errors at once

suites.title: US-0.4: Server-Side Validation of Expense Data

specs.title: The server applies the same rules the client does, even when the client is bypassed
Invalid requests get a 400 with structured error codes
Multiple bad fields come back together in one errors array
Error responses never leak stack traces or internal details
Every expense row offers an Edit button
Clicking Edit populates the form with that expense's current values
Edit mode is clearly signalled — Save Changes label, Cancel button, indicator
Any combination of the three fields can be changed
Saving an edit applies the same validation rules as adding
On save the row updates immediately and the total recalculates
A success indicator confirms the edit and the form leaves edit mode
A Cancel button is visible whenever the form is in edit mode
Cancel discards the pending changes without any server request
The form returns to its add-new state after cancelling
The list and total are unchanged and the original values stay intact

suites.title: US-1.3: Edit Multiple Expenses in Sequence

specs.title: After saving one edit the user can immediately edit another expense
Each edit is persisted independently and the list reflects them all
The running total is correct after several sequential edits

suites.title: US-1.4: Handle Editing a Non-Existent Expense

specs.title: Saving an edit for a vanished expense returns 404 ERR_EXPENSE_NOT_FOUND
The user sees a clear "Expense not found" message
The form keeps the typed data on a 404 so it can be re-entered as a new expense
A malformed expense ID returns 400 ERR_EXPENSE_INVALID_ID
Refreshing the browser still shows every previously entered expense
The list is fetched from the server with GET /api/expenses on page load
The total after a refresh equals the sum of everything persisted
No expense data is kept in localStorage or sessionStorage
Everything submitted is written to the on-disk SQLite file, not held in memory
An edit is written through to disk, so a restart would recover the corrected value
A fresh GET returns exactly what is on disk — the store is the source of truth
No data corruption — every stored row satisfies the schema constraints
The storage file was created automatically — no manual DB setup happened
The schema — expenses table plus its created_at index — exists
The running server detected the existing store rather than re-creating it
A 201 is only returned once the expense is readable from storage
A 200 on update is only returned once the change is readable from storage
A failed save shows "Failed to save expense" and keeps the user's input
Data is stored in a standard, directly-queryable SQLite database
The storage file can be copied for backup and the copy still reads
Each record holds id, amount, description, category, created_at and updated_at
Amounts are stored as integer cents (10.50 becomes 1050)
Timestamps are stored in ISO 8601 UTC format

suites.title: US-3.1: View All Expenses on Page Load

specs.title: Opening the page fetches all expenses from the server
Each row shows the amount as currency plus description and category
Expenses are listed most recent first
Every row carries an Edit button as the entry point for editing
The list is on the main page — no navigation to a separate screen

suites.title: US-3.2: See Empty State When No Expenses Exist

specs.title: With no expenses a friendly, non-technical message is shown
The form stays visible and usable during the empty state
The total reads $0.00 during the empty state
Adding the first expense replaces the empty state with the list

suites.title: US-3.3: List Updates Immediately After Mutations

specs.title: A new expense appears without any page reload
An edited expense shows its new values in the correct row without a reload
Ordering stays most-recent-first after mutations
No duplicate rows appear after add or edit

suites.title: US-3.4: Handle List Loading Errors Gracefully

specs.title: A server 500 shows "Failed to load expenses. Please try again."
An unreachable network shows "Unable to connect to the server."
A Retry option is offered and actually reloads the list
The error state is explicit — not a silently broken or empty list

suites.title: US-3.5: Expense List Performance at Scale

specs.title: A list of 500 expenses renders in under a second with correct amounts
Description and category text is escaped, never executed as HTML
Many entries stay scrollable without breaking the page layout

suites.title: US-4.1: View Running Total of All Expenses

specs.title: The total is prominent and visible without scrolling
The total is formatted as currency with a dollar sign and two decimals
The total is the integer-cents sum of every expense, divided by 100 for display
The total shows $0.00 when no expenses exist

suites.title: US-4.2: Total Updates After Adding an Expense

specs.title: The total increases by exactly the new expense amount, without a reload
The updated total is accurate to the cent across repeated adds
The currency format is unchanged after an update

suites.title: US-4.3: Total Updates After Editing an Expense

specs.title: Editing an amount swaps the old value out and the new value in, no reload
Editing only the description or category leaves the total untouched
The total stays correct through several sequential edits
When the list fails to load the total shows a dash, not a number
No stale total is left behind after a failed refresh
After a successful retry the total displays correctly again
The app opens at its URL with no plugin or install step
The page renders form, list and total together in one layout
Only standard web platform features are used — no plugins or embeds
The app works end to end in this browser engine

suites.title: US-5.2: Single-Page Layout with Clear Hierarchy

specs.title: The form sits prominently near the top of the page
The list sits below the form
The total is visible at the initial scroll position, above the form
Form, list and total are reachable with no tabs, menus or page transitions
Each section is a distinct, labelled region
`npm start` is the single documented command and it runs the server
One origin serves both the static UI and the API
No build step, migration command or config file is needed first
Navigating to the URL immediately shows a working application
PORT is configurable via environment variable and defaults to 3000
The layout is usable at desktop size
The layout stays functional on tablet and phone widths
Focus order runs amount, description, category, then submit
The whole add flow can be driven from the keyboard alone
Pressing Enter in a field submits the form
The Edit and Cancel buttons are reachable and operable by keyboard

suites.title: US-5.5: Graceful Error Handling in the UI

specs.title: Validation errors appear inline next to the field they concern
A server 500 shows "Failed to save expense. Please try again."
A network failure shows "Unable to connect to the server."
An unexpected script error shows "Something went wrong. Please refresh the page."
No error message shown to the user exposes technical details
GET /api/expenses returns 200 with { expenses: [...] }
POST /api/expenses returns 201 with a fully-shaped { expense: {...} }
PUT /api/expenses/:id returns 200 with the updated { expense: {...} }
Error responses use { errors: [...] } for validation and { error: {...} } otherwise
Every field rule maps to its documented ERR_EXPENSE_* code
404 ERR_EXPENSE_NOT_FOUND for a well-formed but unknown id
400 ERR_EXPENSE_INVALID_ID takes precedence over body validation
All validation failures come back in one pass, not one at a time
Dollar amounts convert to integer cents without floating-point drift
The maximum allowed amount stores as 99,999,999 cents
Stored cents round-trip back to the same dollars on the API and on disk
Description and category are trimmed before storage
A whitespace-only description or category is rejected, not trimmed into empty
Script and image payloads in stored text render as inert text
A payload entered through the form is equally inert
Security headers are present on the served page
An empty store returns an empty array rather than null or an error
Boundary lengths and amounts are accepted at the limit and rejected past it
Unicode and emoji survive a round trip intact
A malformed JSON body does not crash the server
Concurrent creates are all persisted with distinct ids
1,000 expenses are served and rendered without breaking
